data.text: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel, heads of their ancestral houses in the line of Tola. They were valiant warriors in their generations; in the days of David they numbered 22,600.
The sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five in all, all of them heads.
With them, according to their generations and ancestral houses, were 36,000 troops ready for war, for they had many wives and sons.
Their relatives from all the clans of Issachar were valiant warriors, 87,000 in all, registered by genealogy.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, five. They were heads of ancestral houses, valiant warriors, with 22,034 registered by genealogy.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were sons of Becher.
Registered by genealogy according to their generations, their heads of ancestral houses and valiant warriors numbered 20,200.
The sons of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these were descendants of Jediael, heads of ancestral houses, valiant warriors; 17,200 could go out with the army to war.
Shuppim and Huppim, descendants of Ir; Hushim, descendants of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, descendants of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom she bore. His Aramean concubine bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife from Huppim and Shuppim. His sister’s name was Maacah. The name of the second was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
Maacah, Machir’s wife, bore a son and named him Peresh. His brother’s name was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eladah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, Ezer, and Elead. The men of Gath who were born in the land killed them because they went down to take their livestock.
Ephraim their father mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He lay with his wife, and she conceived and bore a son. He named him Beriah because disaster had come upon his house.
His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah.
Rephah his son, Resheph, Telah his son, Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, and Joshua his son.
Their possessions and dwelling places were Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages as far as Ayyah and its villages.
data.titulo: Settlements of the Descendants of Joseph

data.text: Along the borders of the descendants of Manasseh were Beth-shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, and Dor and its villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these places.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, with Serah their sister.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were the sons of Japhlet.
The sons of Shamer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
The descendants of his brother Helem: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were descendants of Asher, heads of ancestral houses, choice men, valiant warriors, and leading chiefs. Their number, registered by genealogy for military service in war, was 26,000 men.
